sourceDate.text: 莊宗在魏，與梁戰河上十餘年
莊宗在魏，與梁戰河上十餘年
莊宗常兄事承業，歲時升堂拜母
梁王悉誅唐宦者第五可範等
明宗晚而多病，王淑妃專內
大臣朱弘昭等方圖其事

units.zh: 嗚呼，自古宦、女之禍深矣！
units.en: Alas! Since antiquity the harm done by eunuchs and by women has cut deep.
units.literal: Alas! From antiquity the calamity of eunuchs and women has run deep!

units.zh: 明者未形而知懼，暗者患及而猶安焉，至於亂亡而不可悔也。
units.en: The wise dread disaster before it shows its face; the foolish stay complacent even as ruin approaches—until the state falls and regret comes too late.
units.literal: The clear-sighted fear before the shape appears; the dim remain at ease even when trouble arrives—until disorder and ruin come and nothing can be regretted.

units.zh: 雖然，不可以不戒。
units.en: Even so, the lesson must not be ignored.
units.literal: Even so, one cannot fail to take warning.

units.zh: 作《宦者傳》。
units.en: Hence this “Biographies of Eunuchs.”
units.literal: Thus was composed the “Biographies of Eunuchs.”

units.zh: ○張承業
units.en: ○ Zhang Chengye
units.literal: ○ Zhang Chengye

units.zh: 張承業，字繼元，唐僖宗時宦者也。
units.en: Zhang Chengye, courtesy name Jiyuan, served as a palace eunuch under Tang Xizong.
units.literal: Zhang Chengye, courtesy name Jiyuan, was a eunuch in the time of Emperor Xizong of Tang.

units.zh: 本姓康，幼閹，為內常侍張泰養子。
units.en: Born Kang, he was castrated young and raised by the inner attendant Zhang Tai.
units.literal: His original surname was Kang; castrated in youth, he was adopted by the Inner Regular Attendant Zhang Tai.

units.zh: 晉王兵擊王行瑜，承業數往來兵間，晉王喜其為人。
units.en: When the Prince of Jin campaigned against Wang Xingyu, Chengye shuttled among the armies; the Prince of Jin took a liking to him.
units.literal: When the Prince of Jin’s army attacked Wang Xingyu, Chengye went back and forth among the troops many times; the Prince of Jin was pleased with his character.

units.zh: 及昭宗為李茂貞所迫，將出奔太原，乃先遣承業使晉以道意，因以為河東監軍。
units.en: When Zhaozong, harried by Li Maozhen, prepared to escape to Taiyuan, he sent Chengye ahead to Jin with his message and appointed him Hedong army supervisor.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong, pressed by Li Maozhen, was about to flee to Taiyuan, he first sent Chengye to Jin to convey his intent and made him army supervisor of Hedong.

units.zh: 其後崔胤誅宦官，宦官在外者，悉詔所在殺之。
units.en: After Cui Yin purged the palace eunuchs, every eunuch still in the provinces was ordered killed on sight.
units.literal: Later Cui Yin executed the eunuchs; those outside the capital were all ordered killed wherever they were found.

units.zh: 晉王憐承業，不忍殺，匿之斛律寺。
units.en: The Prince of Jin spared Chengye and hid him at Hulu Temple.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin pitied Chengye and would not kill him, hiding him at Hulu Temple.

units.zh: 昭宗崩，乃出承業，復為監軍。
units.en: After Zhaozong’s death Chengye emerged from hiding and resumed the post of army supervisor.
units.literal: When Zhaozong died, Chengye was brought out and again made army supervisor.

units.zh: 晉王病且革，以莊宗屬承業曰：「以亞子累公等。」
units.en: As the Prince of Jin lay dying he entrusted Zhuangzong to Chengye: “I place Yazi in your hands.”
units.literal: The Prince of Jin, gravely ill, entrusted Zhuangzong to Chengye, saying: “I leave Yazi in your charge.”

units.zh: 莊宗常兄事承業，歲時升堂拜母，甚親重之。
units.en: Zhuangzong treated him like an elder brother, visiting each year to bow to his mother, and held him in the highest regard.
units.literal: Zhuangzong always treated Chengye as an elder brother; each year he went up to the hall to bow to Chengye’s mother and held him in great affection.

units.zh: 莊宗在魏，與梁戰河上十餘年，軍國之事，皆委承業，承業亦盡心不懈。
units.en: For more than ten years Zhuangzong warred with Liang along the Yellow River from Wei; civil and military affairs all went to Chengye, who never slackened in his duty.
units.literal: While Zhuangzong was at Wei fighting Liang on the Yellow River for more than ten years, all military and state affairs were entrusted to Chengye, and Chengye served tirelessly without slackening.

units.zh: 凡所以畜積金粟，收市兵馬，勸課農桑，而成莊宗之業者，承業之功為多。
units.en: The hoarded grain, the armies bought and trained, the fields urged back to the plow—most of what made Zhuangzong’s rise possible was Chengye’s work.
units.literal: Whatever stored grain and gold, mustered troops and horses, urged farming and sericulture, and built Zhuangzong’s enterprise—of that Chengye’s merit was greatest.

units.zh: 自貞簡太后、韓德妃、伊淑妃及諸公子在晉陽者，承業一切以法繩之，權貴皆斂手畏承業。
units.en: Empress Dowager Zhenjian, the consorts Hande and Yishu, the princes at Jinyang—Chengye held them all to the law, and the great families learned to fear him.
units.literal: From Empress Dowager Zhenjian, Consort Hande, Consort Yishu, and all the princes at Jinyang, Chengye bound every one by law; the powerful all shrank back in fear of him.

units.zh: 莊宗歲時自魏歸省親，須錢蒲博、賞賜伶人，而承業主藏，錢不可得。
units.en: When Zhuangzong came home from Wei he wanted coin for dice and to tip the actors; Chengye kept the treasury keys and refused him.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong each year returned from Wei to visit his kin, he needed money for gambling and to reward the actors, but Chengye held the treasury and no cash was to be had.

units.zh: 莊宗乃置酒庫中，酒酣，使子繼岌為承業起舞，舞罷，承業出寶帶、幣、馬為贈，莊宗指錢積呼繼岌小字以語承業曰：「和哥乏錢，可與錢一積，何用帶、馬為也？」
units.en: Zhuangzong held a banquet in the vault. Wine deep, he made his son Jiji dance for Chengye; when the boy finished, Chengye offered a jeweled belt, silks, and a horse. Zhuangzong pointed at the coin stacks and, calling Jiji by his pet name, said to Chengye: “Hege needs money—give him that whole pile. Why offer belt and horse?”
units.literal: Zhuangzong then set wine in the storehouse; when drunk he had his son Jiji dance for Chengye. When the dance ended Chengye brought out a jeweled belt, silks, and a horse as gifts. Zhuangzong pointed at the piled coins and, calling Jiji by his pet name, said to Chengye: “Hege is short of cash—give him this whole pile; what use are belt and horse?”

units.zh: 承業謝曰：「國家錢，非臣所得私也。」
units.en: Chengye answered: “That is the state’s treasury—not mine to give away.”
units.literal: Chengye declined: “This is the state’s money—not something your servant may treat as private.”

units.zh: 莊宗以語侵之，承業怒曰：「臣，老敕使，非為子孫計，惜此庫錢，佐王成霸業爾！
units.en: Zhuangzong sneered; Chengye blazed: “I am an old commissioner of the throne! I am not saving this vault for my heirs—I am saving it to make you king!
units.literal: Zhuangzong’s words grew insulting; Chengye flared: “Your servant is an old commissioner of the throne—not hoarding this vault for his sons and grandsons, but guarding it to help the King build a hegemony!

units.zh: 若欲用之，何必問臣？
units.en: If you mean to spend it, why ask me?
units.literal: If you wish to spend it, why ask me at all?

units.zh: 財盡兵散，豈獨臣受禍也？」
units.en: When the treasury is empty and the army melts away, will I be the only one ruined?”
units.literal: When the wealth is gone and the army scattered, will I alone suffer disaster?”

units.zh: 莊宗顧元行欽曰：「取劍來！」
units.en: Zhuangzong shouted to Yuan Xingqin: “Fetch a sword!”
units.literal: Zhuangzong turned to Yuan Xingqin: “Bring a sword!”

units.zh: 承業起，持莊宗衣而泣，曰：「臣受先王顧托之命，誓雪家國之讎。
units.en: Chengye seized his sleeve and wept: “Your father entrusted you to me—I swore to avenge our house and state.
units.literal: Chengye rose, seized Zhuangzong’s robe, and wept: “Your servant received the late king’s dying charge and swore to wipe out the realm’s enemy.

units.zh: 今日為王惜庫物而死，死不愧於先王矣！」
units.en: If I die today guarding this storehouse, I die with a clear conscience before your father!”
units.literal: Today I die guarding the vault for the King—I die with no shame before the late king!”

units.zh: 閻寶從旁解承業手令去，承業奮拳毆寶踣，罵曰：「閻寶，朱溫之賊，蒙晉厚恩，不能有一言之忠，而反諂諛自容邪！」
units.en: Yan Bao pulled him away; Chengye knocked him flat and raged: “Yan Bao—you were Zhu Wen’s man, Jin fed you honor, and you could not utter one honest word, only flatter and crawl?”
units.literal: Yan Bao stepped in to free Chengye’s hands and make him leave; Chengye struck Bao down with his fist and cursed: “Yan Bao, Zhu Wen’s creature—you enjoyed Jin’s great favor yet could not speak one loyal word, and instead fawn and make room for yourself?”

units.zh: 太后聞之，使召莊宗。
units.en: The empress dowager heard and summoned Zhuangzong.
units.literal: The empress dowager heard and sent for Zhuangzong.

units.zh: 莊宗性至孝，聞太后召，甚懼，乃酌兩卮謝承業曰：「吾杯酒之失，且得罪太后。
units.en: Filial to the bone, he was terrified at the summons. He filled two cups and begged Chengye: “A drunkard’s slip will bring the Dowager’s wrath upon me.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was deeply filial; hearing the dowager’s call he was greatly afraid, poured two cups, and apologized to Chengye: “My fault over a cup of wine will offend the Dowager.

units.zh: 願公飲此，為吾分過。」
units.en: Drink this—forgive me part of the blame.”
units.literal: I beg you drink this and bear part of my fault.”

units.zh: 承業不肯飲。
units.en: Chengye would not touch the cup.
units.literal: Chengye would not drink.

units.zh: 莊宗入內，太后使人謝承業曰：「小兒忤公，已笞之矣。」
units.en: Inside, the dowager sent word: “The boy was rude—I have already had him whipped.”
units.literal: Zhuangzong went inside; the dowager sent word to Chengye: “The boy offended you—I have already beaten him.”

units.zh: 明日，太后與莊宗俱過承業第，慰勞之。
units.en: Next day mother and son came to Chengye’s door to comfort him.
units.literal: The next day the dowager and Zhuangzong both visited Chengye’s house to console him.

units.zh: 盧質嗜酒傲忽，自莊宗及諸公子多見侮慢，莊宗深嫉之。
units.en: Lu Zhi drank hard and treated everyone with contempt; Zhuangzong and the princes smarted under it, and the emperor hated him for it.
units.literal: Lu Zhi was fond of wine and arrogant; from Zhuangzong down to the princes many were insulted by him, and Zhuangzong deeply resented it.

units.zh: 承業乘間請曰：「盧質嗜酒無禮，臣請為王殺之。」
units.en: Chengye seized a moment: “Lu Zhi is drunk and insolent—let me kill him for you.”
units.literal: Chengye seized a moment and said: “Lu Zhi is drunken and without propriety—I beg leave to kill him for the King.”

units.zh: 莊宗曰：「吾方招納賢才以就功業，公何言之過也！」
units.en: Zhuangzong said: “I am recruiting talent to finish the work—your words go too far!”
units.literal: Zhuangzong said: “I am just now gathering worthy men to complete the enterprise—how can you speak so harshly!”

units.zh: 承業起賀曰：「王能如此，天下不足平也！」
units.en: Chengye rose and bowed: “If you can be thus, the realm is already half won!”
units.literal: Chengye rose and congratulated him: “If the King can be thus, the realm is not hard to pacify!”

units.zh: 質因此獲免。
units.en: Lu Zhi was spared.
units.literal: Zhi thereby escaped death.

units.zh: 天祐十八年，莊宗已諾諸將即皇帝位。
units.en: In Tianyou 18 (921) Zhuangzong had already promised his generals the throne.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year of Tianyou, Zhuangzong had already promised the generals he would take the imperial throne.

units.zh: 承業方臥病，聞之，自太原肩輿至魏，諫曰：「大王父子與梁血戰三十年，本欲雪家國之讎，而復唐之社稷。
units.en: Chengye was bedridden; hearing this he was carried from Taiyuan to Wei and pleaded: “Father and son bled against Liang for thirty years to avenge Tang and restore the dynasty.
units.literal: Chengye lay ill; hearing it, he was carried by sedan from Taiyuan to Wei and remonstrated: “King and son have fought Liang in blood for thirty years, intending to avenge house and state and restore Tang’s altars.

units.zh: 今元兇未滅，而遽以尊名自居，非王父子之初心，且失天下望，不可。」
units.en: The chief enemy still lives, yet you seize an emperor’s name—that was never your first vow, and you will lose the world’s heart. You must not.”
units.literal: The chief culprit is not yet destroyed, yet you hasten to take a lofty title for yourself—this is not the King and son’s first intent, and you will lose the world’s hope. It cannot be done.”

units.zh: 莊宗謝曰：「此諸將之所欲也。」
units.en: Zhuangzong said: “The generals demand it.”
units.literal: Zhuangzong apologized: “This is what the generals desire.”

units.zh: 承業曰：「不然，梁，唐、晉之仇賊，而天下所共惡也。
units.en: Chengye said: “No. Liang is Tang’s murderer and Jin’s foe—the world hates it.
units.literal: Chengye said: “Not so. Liang is Tang and Jin’s enemy, hated by all under Heaven.

units.zh: 今王誠能為天下去大惡，復列聖之深讎，然後求唐後而立之。
units.en: Slay that great evil, avenge the Tang emperors, then find a Tang scion and set him on the throne.
units.literal: If the King can truly remove the great evil for the world and avenge the deep wrong of the former emperors, then seek a descendant of Tang and set him on the throne.

units.zh: 使唐之子孫在，孰敢當之？
units.en: If any Tang blood remains, who could stand before you?
units.literal: If Tang’s descendants still live, who would dare stand against you?

units.zh: 使唐無子孫，天下之士，誰可與王爭者？
units.en: If none remain, which man under Heaven could contest you?
units.literal: If Tang has no descendants, which man under Heaven could contend with the King?

units.zh: 臣，唐家一老奴耳，誠願見大王之成功，然後退身田里，使百官送出洛東門，而令路人指而嘆曰『此本朝敕使，先王時監軍也』，豈不臣主俱榮哉？」
units.en: I am only an old slave of Tang. Let me see you triumph, then go home while officials see me out Luoyang’s east gate and folk point and say, “That was the late king’s commissioner”—would not we both be glorified?”
units.literal: Your servant is but an old slave of the Tang house and truly wishes to see the Great King succeed, then retire to the fields, have the hundred officials escort him out Luoyang’s east gate, and let passersby point and sigh, “There goes the dynasty’s commissioner, army supervisor in the late king’s day”—would not lord and minister both be honored?”

units.zh: 莊宗不聽。
units.en: Zhuangzong would not hear him.
units.literal: Zhuangzong would not listen.

units.zh: 承業知不可諫，乃仰天大哭曰：「吾王自取之！
units.en: Knowing words were wasted, Chengye looked skyward and wailed: “My king chooses this for himself!
units.literal: Chengye knew remonstrance was useless, looked up to Heaven and wept loudly: “My king takes it for himself!

units.zh: 誤我奴矣。」
units.en: You have ruined your slave.”
units.literal: You have ruined your old slave.”

units.zh: 肩輿歸太原，不食而卒，年七十七。
units.en: He was carried home to Taiyuan, stopped eating, and died at seventy-seven.
units.literal: He was carried back to Taiyuan, refused food, and died, aged seventy-seven.

units.zh: 同光元年，贈左武衛上將軍，謚曰正憲。
units.en: In Tongguang 1 (923) he was posthumously made General of the Left Martial Guard, posthumous name Zhengxian (“Upright and Lawful”).
units.literal: In the first year of Tongguang he was posthumously made General of the Left Martial Guard; his posthumous title was Zhengxian (“Upright and Lawful”).

units.zh: 張居翰，字德卿，故唐掖廷令張從玫之養子。
units.en: Zhang Juhan, courtesy name Deqing, was the adopted son of Zhang Congmei, a former Tang director of the palace provision bureau.
units.literal: Zhang Juhan, courtesy name Deqing, was the adopted son of Zhang Congmei, former Director of the Palace Provision Bureau under Tang.

units.zh: 昭宗時，為范陽軍監軍，與節度使劉仁恭相善。
units.en: Under Zhaozong he served as army supervisor at Fanyang and was on good terms with the military governor Liu Rengong.
units.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhaozong he served as army supervisor of the Fanyang army and was on good terms with military governor Liu Rengong.

units.zh: 天復中，大誅宦者，仁恭匿居翰大安山之北谿以免。
units.en: During the Tianfu purge of eunuchs, Rengong hid Juhan in a valley north of Mount Da'an to save his life.
units.literal: During Tianfu, when eunuchs were executed on a great scale, Rengong hid Juhan in a valley north of Mount Da'an to escape.

units.zh: 其後，梁兵攻仁恭，仁恭遣居翰從晉王攻梁潞州以牽其兵，晉遂取潞州，以居翰為昭義監軍。
units.en: Later, when Liang attacked Rengong, Rengong sent Juhan with the Prince of Jin against Liang's Luzhou to draw off Liang's army; Jin took Luzhou and appointed Juhan Zhaoyi army supervisor.
units.literal: Later, when Liang troops attacked Rengong, Rengong sent Juhan to follow the Prince of Jin in attacking Liang's Luzhou to draw off their forces; Jin then took Luzhou and made Juhan army supervisor of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 莊宗即位，與郭崇韜並為樞密使。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Juhan and Guo Chongtao were made joint Bureau Commissioners.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he and Guo Chongtao were jointly made Bureau Commissioners.

units.zh: 莊宗滅梁而驕，宦官因以用事，郭崇韜又專任政，居翰默默，茍免而已。
units.en: After Zhuangzong destroyed Liang he grew arrogant; eunuchs took power, Guo Chongtao dominated the government, and Juhan kept quiet, merely trying to stay out of trouble.
units.literal: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and grew arrogant; eunuchs thereby came to power, Guo Chongtao again monopolized government, and Juhan kept silent, merely seeking to escape harm.

units.zh: 魏王破蜀，王衍朝京師，行至秦川，而明宗軍變於魏。
units.en: When the Prince of Wei conquered Shu, Wang Yan set out for the capital; at Qinchuan, Mingzong's troops mutinied at Wei.
units.literal: The Prince of Wei conquered Shu; Wang Yan went to the capital; when they reached Qinchuan, Mingzong's army mutinied at Wei.

units.zh: 莊宗東征，慮衍有變，遣人馳詔魏王殺之。
units.en: Zhuangzong marched east, fearing Yan might turn rebellious, and sent urgent orders to the Prince of Wei to kill him.
units.literal: Zhuangzong marched east, fearing Yan might rebel, and sent a messenger with urgent orders for the Prince of Wei to kill him.

units.zh: 詔書已印畫，而居翰發視之，詔書言「誅衍一行」，居翰以謂殺降不祥，乃以詔傅柱，揩去「行」字，改為一「家」。
units.en: The edict was already sealed, but Juhan opened it and read: "Execute Yan and his whole party." He held that killing surrendered men was ill-omened, pressed the edict to a pillar, wiped out the character for "party," and changed it to "family."
units.literal: The edict was already sealed; but when Juhan opened and read it, the edict said "Execute Yan and his whole party." Juhan held that killing surrendered men was ill-omened, so he pressed the edict against a pillar, wiped away the character for "party," and changed it to "family."

units.zh: 時蜀降人與衍俱東者千餘人，皆獲免。
units.en: More than a thousand Shu men who were traveling east with Yan were all spared.
units.literal: At that time more than a thousand Shu submitters traveling east with Yan were all spared.

units.zh: 莊宗遇弒，居翰見明宗於至德宮，求歸田里。
units.en: After Zhuangzong was assassinated, Juhan met Mingzong at Zhide Palace and asked to return home to the fields.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong was assassinated, Juhan met Mingzong at Zhide Palace and asked to retire to the countryside.

units.zh: 天成三年，卒於長安，年七十一。
units.en: In Tiancheng 3 (928) he died at Chang'an, aged seventy-one.
units.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng he died at Chang'an, aged seventy-one.

units.zh: 五代文章陋矣，而史官之職廢於喪亂，傳記小說多失其傳，故其事跡，終始不完，而雜以訛繆。
units.en: Five Dynasties prose was mean, and the historians’ office collapsed in chaos; tales were lost, deeds break off midstream, and error creeps in.
units.literal: Five Dynasties writing was crude, and the historians’ office collapsed in the turmoil; biographies and tales often lost transmission, so deeds from beginning to end are incomplete and mixed with error.

units.zh: 至於英豪奮起，戰爭勝敗，國家興廢之際，豈無謀臣之略，辯士之談？
units.en: When heroes rose, armies clashed, and kingdoms fell—were there no counsels and no eloquence?
units.literal: When heroes rose, when battles were won or lost, when states rose or fell—were there not strategists’ plans and debaters’ speeches?

units.zh: 而文字不足以發之，遂使泯然無傳於後世。
units.en: Words failed them, and their voices died with the age.
units.literal: Yet words were not enough to bring them forth, and so they vanished without passing to later ages.

units.zh: 然獨張承業事卓卓在人耳目，至今故老猶能道之。
units.en: Yet Zhang Chengye alone stands bright in living memory—old men still tell his story.
units.literal: Yet Zhang Chengye’s deeds alone stand out before men’s eyes; old folk today can still tell them.

units.zh: 其論議可謂傑然歟！
units.en: His counsel was magnificent—was it not?
units.literal: His discourse may be called towering, may it not!

units.zh: 殆非宦者之言也。
units.en: Hardly words one expects from a eunuch.
units.literal: Hardly the speech of a eunuch.

units.zh: 自古宦者亂人之國，其源深於女禍。
units.en: Since antiquity eunuchs have ruined realms—and the root runs deeper than women’s harm.
units.literal: From antiquity eunuchs have thrown states into disorder; the source runs deeper than women’s calamity.

units.zh: 女，色而已；
units.en: Women tempt with beauty alone;
units.literal: Women are but beauty;

units.zh: 宦者之害，非一端也。
units.en: eunuchs harm by many means.
units.literal: the harm of eunuchs is not of one kind alone.

units.zh: 蓋其用事也近而習，其為心也專而忍。
units.en: They serve at the ruler’s side and grow intimate; in heart they are focused and pitiless.
units.literal: They serve near and grow familiar; in heart they are single-minded and cruel.

units.zh: 能以小善中人之意，小信固人之心，使人主必信而親之。
units.en: Small favors win his mood, small loyalties win his trust, until he must believe in them and keep them near.
units.literal: With small kindnesses they hit the ruler’s mood, with small trust they fix his heart, until the sovereign must trust and draw them close.

units.zh: 待其已信，然後懼以禍福而把持之。
units.en: Then they bind him with fear of rise and ruin and take the reins.
units.literal: Once he trusts them, they then frighten him with fortune and disaster and seize control.

units.zh: 雖有忠臣碩士列於朝廷，而人主以為去己疏遠，不若起居飲食、前後左右之親為可恃也。
units.en: Loyal ministers may fill the court, yet the ruler thinks them far from himself—not so reliable as those at his pillow and table.
units.literal: Though loyal ministers and great scholars stand in court, the ruler thinks them distant from himself and not so dependable as those close at rising, eating, before and behind.

units.zh: 故前後左右者日益親，則忠臣碩士日益疏，而人主之勢日益孤。
units.en: Those at his side draw closer; his ministers draw farther; his power stands alone.
units.literal: Thus those before and behind grow daily closer, loyal ministers daily more remote, and the ruler’s position daily more isolated.

units.zh: 勢孤，則懼禍之心日益切，而把持者日益牢。
units.en: Alone, he fears ruin more each day; their grip tightens each day.
units.literal: Isolated, fear of disaster grows daily keener, and those who hold control grow daily firmer.

units.zh: 安危出其喜怒，禍患伏於帷闥，則向之所謂可恃者，乃所以為患也。
units.en: His fate rides on their moods; peril hides behind the curtain—the “dependable” become the danger.
units.literal: Safety and danger issue from their pleasure and anger; disaster hides within the bed-curtains—then those once called dependable become the source of harm.

units.zh: 患已深而覺之，欲與疏遠之臣圖左右之親近，緩之則養禍而益深，急之則挾人主以為質，雖有聖智不能與謀，謀之而不可為，為之而不可成，至其甚，則俱傷而兩敗。
units.en: When he wakes to the poison and turns to distant ministers against his intimates—move slowly and the rot spreads; move fast and they hold him hostage. Even a sage cannot plot freely: plans fail, action fails—until ruler and realm break together.
units.literal: When the harm is deep and he awakens, wishing to plot with distant ministers against close intimates—if he is slow, he nourishes disaster and it deepens; if he is hasty, they hold the ruler as hostage. Though he has sage wisdom none can counsel with him; counsel cannot be acted on, action cannot succeed—at the extreme both sides are wounded and both fail.

units.zh: 故其大者亡國，其次亡身，而使奸豪得借以為資而起，至抉其種類，盡殺以快天下之心而後已。
units.en: The worst end in ruined states, the lesser in ruined men; rebels use the backlash to rise, hunt every eunuch, and kill until the crowd is satisfied.
units.literal: Thus the great cases destroy the state, the lesser destroy the person, and treacherous heroes seize the occasion to rise, until they root out the whole breed and slaughter all to satisfy the world’s heart before stopping.

units.zh: 此前史所載宦者之禍常如此者，非一世也。
units.en: So runs the eunuch plague in the old histories—not once alone.
units.literal: This is how eunuch calamity in former histories usually runs—not for one age alone.

units.zh: 夫為人主者，非欲養禍於內而疏忠臣碩士於外，蓋其漸積而勢使之然也。
units.en: No ruler chooses inner ruin and outer exile of his best men—circumstance piles up until he has no choice.
units.literal: Rulers do not wish to nourish disaster within and keep loyal ministers afar; gradual accumulation and circumstance make it so.

units.zh: 夫女色之惑，不幸而不悟，則禍斯及矣，使其一悟，捽而去之可也。
units.en: A woman’s charm: if he never wakes, he is lost; wake once and he can cast her off.
units.literal: Women’s allure—if unlucky he does not awaken, disaster reaches him; if he awakens once, he can seize and cast her out.

units.zh: 宦者之為禍，雖欲悔悟，而勢有不得而去也，唐昭宗之事是已。
units.en: Eunuch harm—even repentance may not let him escape; Zhaozong proved that.
units.literal: Eunuch harm—even wishing to repent, circumstance may not allow removal; Emperor Zhaozong’s affair is proof.

units.zh: 故曰深於女禍者，謂此也。
units.en: That is what “deeper than women’s harm” means.
units.literal: Thus “deeper than women’s calamity” means this.

units.zh: 可不戒哉！
units.en: Who would not take warning?
units.literal: Can one fail to take warning!

units.zh: 昭宗信狎宦者，由是有東宮之幽。
units.en: Zhaozong doted on his eunuchs—and the crown prince was imprisoned.
units.literal: Zhaozong trusted and played with eunuchs; hence the Eastern Palace’s confinement.

units.zh: 既出而與崔胤圖之，胤為宰相，顧力不足為，乃召兵於梁。
units.en: Freed, he plotted with Chancellor Cui Yin, who lacked force and summoned Liang’s troops.
units.literal: After he escaped he plotted with Cui Yin; Yin was chancellor but saw his strength insufficient, and so called in Liang’s army.

units.zh: 梁兵且至，而宦者挾天子走之岐。
units.en: As Liang marched, the eunuchs dragged the emperor west to Qi.
units.literal: Liang’s army was about to arrive, and the eunuchs carried the Son of Heaven away to Qi.

units.zh: 梁兵圍之三年，昭宗既出，而唐亡矣。
units.en: Three years of siege; when Zhaozong emerged, Tang was dead.
units.literal: Liang besieged three years; when Zhaozong came out, Tang was finished.

units.zh: 初，昭宗之出也，梁王悉誅唐宦者第五可範等七百餘人，其在外者，悉詔天下捕殺之，而宦者多為諸鎮所藏匿而不殺。
units.en: When Zhaozong fled, the Liang king slaughtered seven hundred Tang eunuchs including Diwu Kefan; the rest were ordered killed empire-wide, yet governors hid many.
units.literal: At first, when Zhaozong fled, the Liang king executed more than seven hundred Tang eunuchs including Diwu Kefan; those outside were ordered hunted throughout the realm, yet many were hidden by military governors and not killed.

units.zh: 是時，方鎮僭擬，悉以宦官給事，而吳越最多。
units.en: Provinces defied the center and staffed their courts with eunuchs—Wu and Yue most of all.
units.literal: Then the provinces usurped authority and all used eunuchs in service; Wu and Yue had the most.

units.zh: 及莊宗立，詔天下訪求故唐時宦者悉送京師，得數百人，宦者遂復用事，以至於亡。
units.en: Zhuangzong recalled Tang eunuchs to the capital by the hundreds; they took power again—and the house fell.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong rose he ordered a search for Tang eunuchs to be sent to the capital; several hundred were found, eunuchs again held power, and ruin followed.

units.zh: 此何異求已覆之車，躬駕而履其轍也？
units.en: What is this but finding an overturned cart and driving it back along the same rut?
units.literal: What difference from seeking an overturned cart, then yoking it and driving over the same rut?

units.zh: 可為悲夫！
units.en: A bitter lesson.
units.literal: Pitiable indeed!

units.zh: 莊宗未滅梁時，承業已死。
units.en: Before Liang fell, Chengye was already dead.
units.literal: Before Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Chengye was already dead.

units.zh: 其後居翰雖為樞密使，而不用事。
units.en: Juhan later became Bureau Commissioner in name only.
units.literal: Afterward Juhan was made Bureau Commissioner but held no real power.

units.zh: 有宣徽使馬紹宏者，嘗賜姓李，頗見信用。
units.en: Palace Commissioner Ma Shaohong, once given the Li surname, won real favor.
units.literal: There was the Palace Commissioner Ma Shaohong, once granted the surname Li, who enjoyed considerable trust.

units.zh: 然誣殺大臣，黷貨賂，專威福，以取怨於天下者，左右狎匿，黃門內養之徒也。
units.en: Yet the men who framed ministers, sold offices, and hoarded power until the realm hated them were the emperor’s cronies—the inner attendants of the yellow gate.
units.literal: Yet those who slandered and killed great ministers, took bribes, and monopolized favor to earn the world’s hatred were the close intimates, the yellow-gate inner attendants.

units.zh: 是時，明宗自鎮州入覲，奉朝請於京師。
units.en: Mingzong had come from Zhenzhou to court and waited in the capital as a mere courtier.
units.literal: At that time Mingzong came from Zhenzhou to attend court and waited in the capital as a courtier.

units.zh: 莊宗頗疑其有異志，陰遣紹宏伺其動靜，紹宏反以情告明宗。
units.en: Zhuangzong suspected him and sent Shaohong to spy; Shaohong warned Mingzong instead.
units.literal: Zhuangzong suspected disloyalty and secretly sent Shaohong to watch him; Shaohong instead told Mingzong what he knew.

units.zh: 明宗自魏而反，天下皆知禍起於魏，孰知其啟明宗之二心者，自紹宏始也！
units.en: When Mingzong rebelled from Wei the world blamed Wei—few knew Shaohong planted the seed.
units.literal: When Mingzong rose from Wei in rebellion, all knew disaster began at Wei—who knew that what opened Mingzong’s second thoughts began with Shaohong!

units.zh: 郭崇韜已破蜀，莊宗信宦者言而疑之。
units.en: Guo Chongtao had taken Shu; Zhuangzong, believing the eunuchs, turned against him.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao had already conquered Shu; Zhuangzong believed the eunuchs’ words and doubted him.

units.zh: 然崇韜之死，莊宗不知，皆宦者為之也。
units.en: Chongtao died without Zhuangzong’s knowledge—the eunuchs killed him.
units.literal: Yet Chongtao’s death Zhuangzong did not know—the eunuchs did it all.

units.zh: 當此之時，舉唐之精兵皆在蜀，使崇韜不死，明宗入洛，豈無西顧之患？
units.en: Tang’s best troops were still in Shu; had Chongtao lived, would Mingzong have dared march on Luoyang without glancing west?
units.literal: At that time all Tang’s elite troops were in Shu; if Chongtao had lived, when Mingzong entered Luoyang would there not have been worry over the west?

units.zh: 其能晏然取唐而代之邪？
units.en: Could he have calmly seized the throne?
units.literal: Could he calmly have taken Tang and replaced it?

units.zh: 及明宗入立，又詔天下悉捕宦者而殺之。
units.en: Mingzong’s first order was another empire-wide slaughter of eunuchs.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he again ordered eunuchs hunted and killed throughout the realm.

units.zh: 宦者亡竄山谷，多削髮為浮圖。
units.en: They fled to the hills and shaved their heads as monks.
units.literal: Eunuchs fled into mountain valleys; many shaved their heads and became monks.

units.zh: 其亡至太原者七十餘人，悉捕而殺之都亭驛，流血盈庭。
units.en: Seventy who reached Taiyuan were seized and killed at Duting Post until the courtyard ran with blood.
units.literal: More than seventy who reached Taiyuan were all seized and killed at Duting Post; blood filled the courtyard.

units.zh: 明宗晚而多病，王淑妃專內以幹政，宦者孟漢瓊因以用事。
units.en: Mingzong aged and fell ill; Consort Wang Shufei ruled within, and eunuch Meng Hanqiong seized the levers.
units.literal: When Mingzong grew old and ill, Consort Wang Shufei meddled within the palace, and the eunuch Meng Hanqiong thereby came to power.

units.zh: 秦王入視明宗疾已革，既出而聞哭聲，以謂帝崩矣，乃謀以兵入宮者，懼不得立也。
units.en: The Prince of Qin visited the dying emperor; leaving, he heard lamentation, thought his father dead, and plotted to storm the palace lest he lose the throne.
units.literal: The Prince of Qin entered to see Mingzong’s illness already grave; after he left he heard weeping and thought the emperor had died, and so plotted to enter the palace with troops—fearing he would not be enthroned.

units.zh: 大臣朱弘昭等方圖其事，議未決，漢瓊遽入見明宗，言秦王反，即以兵誅之，陷秦王大惡，而明宗以此飲恨而終。
units.en: Ministers Zhu Hongzhao and others still debated; Hanqiong rushed to the sickbed, cried treason, and had the Prince of Qin killed—loading him with guilt so that Mingzong died in bitterness.
units.literal: Ministers Zhu Hongzhao and the rest were just plotting the matter when the decision was not yet made; Hanqiong hurried in to see Mingzong, said the Prince of Qin had rebelled, and at once used troops to execute him, casting the great blame on the prince so that Mingzong died nursing hatred.

units.zh: 後湣帝奔於衛州，漢瓊西迎廢帝於路，廢帝惡而殺之。
units.en: Later, when Emperor Min fled to Weizhou, Hanqiong went west to meet the deposed emperor on the road; the deposed emperor despised him and had him killed.
units.literal: Later, when Emperor Min fled to Weizhou, Hanqiong went west to meet the deposed emperor on the road; the deposed emperor hated him and had him killed.

units.zh: 嗚呼！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 人情處安樂，自非聖哲，不能久而無驕怠。
units.en: Ease and comfort spoil every man who is not a sage—pride and slackness follow.
units.literal: Human feeling in ease and pleasure—unless one is a sage, cannot long go without pride and slackness.

units.zh: 宦、女之禍非一日，必伺人之驕怠而浸入之。
units.en: Eunuchs and women do not strike in a day—they wait until pride and idleness open the door.
units.literal: The calamity of eunuchs and women is not of a day; they must wait for a man’s pride and slackness to seep in.

units.zh: 明宗非佚君，而猶若此者，蓋其在位差久也。
units.en: Mingzong was no wastrel—yet even he fell prey, perhaps because he reigned too long.
units.literal: Mingzong was no idle ruler, yet even so—perhaps because he reigned rather long.

units.zh: 其餘多武人崛起，及其嗣續，世數短而年不永，故宦者莫暇施為。
units.en: Most other rulers were soldiers who rose overnight; their lines were brief, and eunuchs barely had time to work harm.
units.literal: The rest were mostly military men who rose suddenly; when their lines continued, generations were few and years short, so eunuchs had no room to act.

units.zh: 其為大害者，略可見矣。
units.en: Where the worst happened, the pattern is plain enough.
units.literal: Where the great harm occurred, it can be seen in outline.

units.zh: 獨承業之論，偉然可愛，而居翰更一字以活千人。
units.en: Chengye’s counsel stands noble and bright; Juhan changed one character in an edict and spared a thousand lives.
units.literal: Chengye’s discourse alone is lofty and lovable, and Juhan by changing one character saved a thousand lives.

units.zh: 君子之於人也，茍有善焉，無所不取，吾於斯二人者，有所取焉。
units.en: The noble take whatever good they find in a man; from these two I take what is good.
units.literal: The noble man toward others, if there is good in them, takes it without stint; in these two men I take something.

units.zh: 取其善而戒其惡，所謂「愛而知其惡，憎而知其善」也。
units.en: Cherish the good and heed the evil—that is “to love yet see the fault, to hate yet see the virtue.”
units.literal: Take the good and warn against the evil—this is what is called “love yet know their evil, hate yet know their good.”

units.zh: 故並述其禍敗之所以然者著於篇。
units.en: So both are told here, with the causes of their ruin set down in full.
units.literal: Therefore both are set forth together, with the reasons calamity and ruin came to be written in this chapter.
